test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The speed of a boat going downstream is 22 km/h. The speed of the stream is 1 km/h. How much distance in total will the boat cover going 3 hours downstream and 2 hours upstream?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of boat going downstream = 22 km/h

Speed of stream = 1 km/h

**Concept Used:**

Speed of stream = (1)/(2)(Downstream Speed – Upstream Speed)

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

Putting the values in the formula,

⇒ 1 = (1)/(2)(22 – Upstream speed)

⇒ 2 = 22 – Upstream speed

Upstream speed = 22 – 2 = 20 km/h

Now, for downstream distance travelled in 3 hours,

⇒ 22 = (Distance)/(3)

Distance = 22 × 3 = 66 km

For upstream distance travelled in 2 hours,

⇒ 20 = (Distance)/(2)

Distance = 20 × 2 = 40 km

Total distance travelled both upstream and downstream = 66 + 40 = 106 km

**Hence, the total distance covered by boat is 106 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**we know upstream speed = x - y and downstream speed = x + y

Where x is speed of boat and y is speed of stream

Given that x + y = 22km/hr and speed of stream y = 1 km/hr

So, x = 22 - 1 = 21 km/hr

Distance = Speed × Time

Total distance = 3 (x + y) + 2 (x - y) = 5x + y

using the above value of x and y

Total distance = 5 × 21 + 1 = 106 km
